what: The heuristic precomputes customer/depot mappings from goal and fact names, compact location/visited fact encodings, and a directed routing-cost matrix reconstructed from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator metric costs. It also performs exact-name, best-effort lookup of load, vehicles, capacity, maximum vehicles, and customer demands, using permissive defaults when static resource fluents were folded away. At evaluation, it finds the current location and unvisited customers, reads dynamic load/vehicle values, applies a necessary aggregate capacity feasibility test when possible, then constructs a capacity-aware nearest-neighbour completion that closes routes at the depot when necessary. The final value is 90% of this greedy completion cost plus 10% of a current-to-customers-to-depot spanning-tree connection estimate.
why: CVRP states are dominated by routing geometry, current route position, residual capacity, and the cost of future depot returns. Grounded operators provide a robust, translator-independent source of all routing costs, while the goal facts provide a general customer set without hardcoded names or counts. A greedy feasible completion is intentionally non-admissible but gives a much sharper estimate and stronger successor ordering than a pure MST bound. The small spanning-tree component stabilizes the estimate against nearest-neighbour artifacts. Capacity-aware route splitting is especially useful for the representative instances, where multiple tightly constrained routes are required, while permissive resource defaults preserve a useful routing heuristic when capacity or demand variables have been folded into derived expressions.
